source: MCPEvol-Bench paper v1 and pinned execution source at commit 888c779a0fe735f612ca62bdd1fdd7c9e6bf8701
setting: MCPEvol-Bench agent execution on the current mutation-stage MCP server

fields: tool-role message associated with the call
at most the first 500 characters of the stringified result
mcpevol_declared_artifacts.phase: after a call and before a later model request

mcpevol_declared_artifacts.artifact: agent conversation history and bounded continuation
fields: later tool calls until stop or max_round

verified old-version trace supplied to the agent

observable_derivation_rules.rule: A target literal explicitly present in the current method-facing schema, description, task, or visible execution message is observable in that surface.
No value may be credited as an old-trace source because the runner does not place the old tool call trace in the agent messages.
The source register may identify a mutation for this audit, but it is not treated as information granted to the evaluated agent.

fail_closed_rule: If a target is not a declared field, or if a required construction convention is not evidenced by the declared surface, classify it as unreachable rather than infer a likely convention.

rights_conclusion.basis: The paper states that the agent state is initialized from the server description including input schemas and semantic descriptions, and that tool execution results are observations. The pinned runner passes current tool definitions into ChatModel and the pinned agent appends tool results/errors to the next request. It does not pass an old schema or old trace.
rights_conclusion.uncertainty: The public paper HTML does not expose the full H.3 prompt text; the executable runner and agent source establish the tool/schema, feedback, and retry surfaces.
